### Fixed
- **`spec.headers` reach a person's session connection.** An MCPServer's `spec.headers` were sent by the server-level client only; the connection muster opens for a person's session to an OAuth server (the person's grant as bearer, a forwarded login token, a token exchanged for it) sent none of them. The hosted GitHub MCP server selects its toolsets per session from `X-MCP-Toolsets`, so with `spec.headers: {X-MCP-Toolsets: default,git}` on the `github` MCPServer the server-level probe saw the `git` toolset while every person's session connected with the default 48 tools and `x_github_get_repository_tree` was "tool not found". The headers now travel with the pending-auth registration into the aggregator's registry, next to `spec.meta` and `spec.timeout`, and every session-scoped client sends them on the handshake and on every call; the session's `Authorization` header stays its own, an entry of that name in the definition is left out. A change of `spec.headers` on a live definition closes the connections the sessions hold to the server the way an auth configuration change does (`session_auth_reset`, `changed: headers`), tools kept resolvable; a session's next call reconnects with the grant it still holds, and that connection carries the new set. Scenario `oauth-session-client-sends-definition-headers`; the mock backend's tools gained `echo_headers` and a pre-configured mock's config a `headers` field for the definition. ([#1304](https://github.com/giantswarm/muster/issues/1304))
